bib.title: BERT for Joint Intent Classification and Slot Filling

question: Does fine-tuning pre-trained BERT as one joint intent classifier and slot filler beat RNN and slot-gated joint models on ATIS and Snips?
hypothesis: BERT pre-training addresses the poor generalization of NLU models trained on small labelled data, and joint modelling of intent and slots helps further.
contributions: we explore the BERT pre-trained model to address the poor generalization capability of NLU

we propose a joint intent classification and slot filling model based on BERT and demonstrate that the proposed model achieves significant improvement on intent classification accuracy, slot filling F1, and sentence-level semantic frame accuracy on several public benchmark datasets

method.summary: Fine-tune English uncased BERT-Base end to end with a softmax intent head on the [CLS] hidden state and a softmax slot head on the first sub-token of each word, minimising summed cross-entropy. A variant replaces the slot softmax with a CRF.

training.objective: maximize p(y_i, y_s | x) = p(y_i|x) * prod_n p(y_s_n|x); fine-tuned end-to-end by minimising cross-entropy loss

limits: Baseline numbers are copied from Goo et al. (2018), not re-run; no variance, seeds or significance test, yet 'significantly outperform' is claimed.
Conclusion says joint BERT beats BERT modelling the tasks separately, but the ablation is on Snips only.
No ablation without BERT pre-training, so the gain cannot be split between pretraining and joint head.
The Wikipedia explanation for the case study (Table 4) is a single example and 'possibly' speculation.
Authors list evaluation on larger, more complex NLU datasets as future work.
Epoch count for ATIS and the sentence-accuracy definition are not stated.
